In [[mathematics]], the '''analytic Fredholm theorem''' is a result concerning the existence of [[bounded linear operator|bounded]] [[inverse function|inverse]]s for a family of bounded linear operators on a [[Hilbert space]]. It is the basis of two classical and important theorems, the [[Fredholm alternative]] and the [[Hilbert–Schmidt theorem]]. The result is named after the [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[mathematician]] [[Erik Ivar Fredholm]].

==Statement of the theorem==

Let {{math|''G'' ⊆ '''C'''}} be a domain (an [[open set|open]] and [[connected space|connected set]]). Let {{math|(''H'', ⟨ , ⟩)}} be a [[real number|real]] or [[complex number|complex]] Hilbert space and let Lin(''H'') denote the space of [[bounded linear operator]]s from ''H'' into itself; let '''I''' denote the [[identity operator]]. Let {{math|''B'' : ''G'' → Lin(''H'')}} be a mapping such that

* ''B'' is analytic on ''G'' in the sense that the [[limit (mathematics)|limit]] <math display="block">\lim_{\lambda \to \lambda_{0}} \frac{B(\lambda) - B(\lambda_{0})}{\lambda - \lambda_{0}}</math> exists for all {{math|''λ''<sub>0</sub> ∈ ''G''}}; and
* the operator ''B''(''λ'') is a [[compact operator]] for each {{math|''λ'' ∈ ''G''}}.

Then either

* {{math|('''I''' − ''B''(''λ''))<sup>−1</sup>}} does not exist for any {{math|''λ'' ∈ ''G''}}; or
* {{math|('''I''' − ''B''(''λ''))<sup>−1</sup>}} exists for every {{math|''λ'' ∈ ''G'' \ ''S''}}, where ''S'' is a [[discrete set|discrete subset]] of ''G'' (i.e., ''S'' has no [[limit point]]s in ''G''). In this case, the function taking ''λ'' to {{math|('''I''' − ''B''(''λ''))<sup>−1</sup>}} is analytic on {{math|''G'' \ ''S''}} and, if {{math|''λ'' ∈ ''S''}}, then the equation <math display="block">B(\lambda) \psi = \psi</math> has a finite-dimensional family of solutions.
